doc.title: Oliver Nelson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 10, 2020

title: Degrees, energy-sector jobs and returning to music
summary: Nelson Jr. recounts his bachelor's, master's in classical flute and doctorate, with years teaching and working in energy auditing and a gas utility between.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Oh yeah, let me give you a little history of me. I got my bachelor’s degree in 1977 in music education. Twenty years later I got my master’s degree in classical flute performance. I studied with the principal in the Indianapolis Symphony here, and then nineteen years later I decided to go back and get my doctorate at the University of Illinois where I studied with Chip McNeil. So my career has been very varied. In between those times I taught for one year at the Indianapolis Public Schools and I said, well teachers don’t make a lot of money, I need to do something else. So I went into the energy field. I didn’t even know how to spell energy, Monk. So we were doing energy audits on different facilities around the state of Indiana. I did that for five years for the state. Then I worked for twelve years for the local gas utility, Citizen’s Gas here in Indianapolis, and they paid for me to get my master’s in classical flute performance at Butler University here, which was really a blessing, it was really cool.
